title: Count Binface receives over a quarter of votes in Clacton by-election
summary:
Count Binface, the satirical candidate and self-styled "intergalactic space warrior," achieved his best-ever election result in the Clacton by-election, receiving 9,455 votes (26.9%). Reform UK leader Nigel Farage won the seat with 63.3% (22,239 votes), after triggering the by-election by resigning and running again, which led to a boycott by other major parties.

Binface is the alter ego of comedian Jon Harvey, a writer for BBC shows including *The Thick of It*. He first stood in 2017 as Lord Buckethead against Theresa May, winning 249 votes. He later took on Boris Johnson in 2019 (69 votes), Rishi Sunak in 2024 (308 votes), and Andy Burnham in 2026 (95 votes) before his strong Clacton finish.

The article highlights the UK tradition of novelty and spoof candidates, tracing it back to Screaming Lord Sutch and the Monster Raving Loony Party. It notes that candidates only need £500 and 10 signatures to stand, though the deposit is lost if they fail to secure 5% of the vote—Binface has lost his deposit every time. These candidates aim to mock power, puncture political pomposity, and offer protest votes. The piece also mentions the tradition of all candidates standing together on stage at election counts, which gives even a "bloke dressed as a bin" an equal moment in the spotlight.

title: Seven books I keep close because I love them
summary:
Mark Dominus describes seven books kept on the shelf nearest his desk, chosen not for frequent reference alone but for the inspiration he hopes they will impart. The article covers several:

- **Roget’s Thesaurus (4th edition)**: He defends Roget against the misconception that it’s just a synonym finder. It is a conceptual hierarchy organizing ideas by category, helping writers refine meaning and discover related concepts. He tried the 8th edition but found it too bulky and less suited to his needs.

- **The Prose of Sir Thomas Browne**: Browne’s Baroque-era writing appeals to Dominus for its wit, learning, wisdom, and humane curiosity. He admires Browne’s willingness to investigate the world joyfully, as seen in *Pseudodoxia Epidemica*, and hopes the book will inspire a renewed interest in Browne.

- **Boccaccio’s Decameron**: Written in 1348 against the backdrop of the Black Death, it tells of ten young people leaving plague-stricken Florence to tell stories. Dominus contrasts its human-centered, practical spirit with Dante’s medieval worldview. He praises the Cormac Ó Cuilleanáin translation and mentions favorite and funny stories.

- **From Frege to Gödel, edited by van Heijenoort**: A collection of foundational papers in mathematical logic, from Frege’s *Begriffsschrift* to Gödel. Dominus notes key contributions by Russell, Peano, Zermelo, Ackermann, and others. He also shares trivia: van Heijenoort was Trotsky’s secretary and one of Frida Kahlo’s lovers.

The article begins describing these as part of a seven-book shelf, but only these are detailed before the text cuts off.

title: RustDesk now supports true unattended remote access on Wayland
summary: RustDesk has introduced true unattended remote access for Wayland, eliminating the need for someone at the remote machine to approve each session. title: Why does Opus 5 feel worse to work with?
summary:
Opus 5 feels worse to work with despite being more capable than Opus 4.7, 4.8, and Fable. The author and colleagues find that these other models ask clarifying questions when intent is unclear, avoid making assumptions, and don’t reinterpret plans without permission. Opus 5 requires careful babysitting because it lacks these behaviors.

The author speculates this stems from two forces: the pursuit of self-improving AI, and pressure to score well on benchmarks. Benchmark tasks are typically self-contained and solvable without asking questions, so models that make bold, usually-correct assumptions in ambiguity are rewarded, while those that stop to ask are penalized.

However, real-world coding agents face incomplete context—business goals, budgets, and intentions are rarely fully written down. In such situations, users want an agent that recognizes ambiguity and asks rather than guessing, since real-life consequences are high. The article concludes that benchmark optimization inherently conflicts with what most people need from a coding agent: a willingness to pause and seek clarification.
chinese_title: 为什么 Opus 5 用起来感觉更差？
chinese_summary:
尽管 Opus 5 比 Opus 4.7、4.8 和 Fable 能力更强，但用起来感觉更差。作者和同事发现，这些其他模型在意图不明确时会提出澄清问题，避免做出假设，并且不会未经允许重新解释计划。Opus 5 需要小心看护，因为它缺乏这些行为。

作者推测这源于两股力量：对自我改进 AI 的追求，以及在基准测试中取得高分的压力。基准测试任务通常是自包含的，无需提问即可解决，因此那些在模糊情况下做出大胆且通常正确的假设的模型会得到奖励，而那些停下来提问的模型则会受到惩罚。

然而，现实世界中的编程代理面临不完整的上下文——业务目标、预算和意图很少被完整地写下来。在这种情况下，用户希望代理能够识别模糊性并提问，而不是猜测，因为现实生活中的后果很严重。文章总结道，基准优化本质上与大多数人对编程代理的需求相冲突：人们需要的是愿意停下来寻求澄清的代理。

title: Google is making private AI practical with homomorphic encryption
summary:
Google has introduced HEIR (Homomorphic Encryption Intermediate Representation), an open-source compiler designed to make private AI inference practical through homomorphic encryption (HE). HE allows computations to be performed directly on encrypted data, so servers can process user information without ever seeing it—balancing privacy with functionality. This shifts the capability/privacy trade-off from a security dilemma to a question of computational cost, which is rapidly decreasing.

HEIR aims to be a one-click solution for developers, automatically converting pre-trained AI models to operate on encrypted inputs, eliminating the need for expert cryptographers. Since 2023, Google has partnered with hardware accelerators (Belfort, Niobium, Cornami, Optalysys) and collaborated with universities like Georgia Tech, CMU, and Tsinghua. Four peer-reviewed publications have already been built on HEIR.

The article showcases four private inference applications compiled with HEIR, running on single-threaded CPU:
1. A Deep Learning Recommendation Model (with Belfort Labs, LG, NYU)
2. Credit card fraud detection (with Niobium and hardshell.ai)
3. Kitsune network intrusion/anomaly detection (with Niobium)
4. A hotword detection model for audio-triggered AI (with Belfort Labs)

These demos demonstrate HE’s real-world viability across content recommendations, fraud prevention, and privacy-preserving network/audio analysis. Google positions HEIR as part of its broader private computing toolkit, alongside differential privacy and private information retrieval, and is working to make homomorphic encryption easy to develop, fast, and ubiquitous across industry.

title: How Claude's text watermarking works
summary:
Anthropic will watermark text from future Claude models to comply with the EU AI Act, which requires marking AI-generated content. The method, based on Google DeepMind’s SynthID-Text approach, subtly alters the random choices Claude makes between equally valid words (e.g., “overcast” vs. “grey”) to embed a detectable pattern. This watermark does not affect output quality, readability, or creativity, adds no hidden characters, requires no extra tokens, and does not slow the model or increase cost. It carries no user-identifying information and cannot be traced to individuals or organizations.

Watermarking works best on longer, more creative passages; it is sparse in factual or exact contexts (like code or solving math problems) where word choice is constrained. When Claude proofreads human text, the watermark may be too weak to detect since most words are the user’s. Translations, where Claude chooses every word, are watermarked. Code contains minimal watermarking except in arbitrary areas like comments.

Detection will be offered via an upcoming API. The watermark only indicates the likelihood Claude was involved; it cannot prove human authorship or attribute ownership. Light editing may not remove it, but a full rewrite will. For images and other files, Claude will attach C2PA content credentials in metadata—an industry standard—rather than an embedded watermark. Older Claude models will gain watermarking over a transition period. This method differs from AI detection software like Pangram, which relies on stylistic “tells” rather than a cryptographic key.
chinese_title: Claude的文本水印是如何工作的
chinese_summary:
Anthropic将为未来的Claude模型生成的文本添加水印，以遵守欧盟《人工智能法案》的要求，该法案规定必须对AI生成的内容进行标记。该方法基于Google DeepMind的SynthID-Text技术，通过微妙地改变Claude在同等合理的词语之间（例如“阴天”与“灰色”）的随机选择，来嵌入可检测的模式。该水印不会影响输出质量、可读性或创意，不添加隐藏字符，不消耗额外token，也不会降低模型速度或增加成本。它不携带任何可识别用户身份的信息，无法追溯到个人或组织。

水印在较长、更具创造性的文本中效果最佳；在事实性或精确性语境中（如代码或数学题解答），由于词语选择受限，水印较为稀疏。当Claude校对人类文本时，水印可能过于微弱而难以检测，因为大部分词语是用户自己的。翻译文本中，由于每个词都由Claude选择，因此会被添加水印。代码中包含极少的水印，仅在注释等任意区域有所体现。

检测功能将通过即将推出的API提供。水印仅表明Claude参与生成的可能性，不能证明人类 authorship 或归属权。轻度编辑可能无法去除水印，但完全重写可以去除。对于图像和其他文件，Claude将在元数据中附加C2PA内容凭证——这是一种行业标准——而非嵌入式水印。较老版本的Claude模型将在过渡期内逐步获得水印功能。该方法不同于Pangram等AI检测软件，后者依赖风格上的“痕迹”而非加密密钥。

title: Introducing Toast 1
summary:
Toast 1 is a specialised search agent released by Mixedbread, designed to match frontier models like Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on retrieval tasks while being up to 10× cheaper and 12× faster. It can run standalone or as a subagent for generalist frontier models, taking over the full search loop: decomposing queries, gathering evidence, inspecting sources, and curating context.

Key results:
- On Databricks' OfficeQA Pro V2, GPT-5.6 Sol with Toast 1 in Codex reached 70% answer correctness at ~$1.15 per task, setting a new state-of-the-art. Claude Fable 5 on Genie scored 60% at ~$4; GPT-5.6 Sol without Toast 1 scored only 33%.
- On Harvey LAB's firm-knowledge benchmark, adding Toast 1 as a subagent cut token use from 80.6M (vanilla) to 23M while maintaining the same score of 55 — a 3.5× token reduction and 60% cost saving.
- In standalone deep search, Toast 1 matches frontier models on benchmarks like BrowseComp Plus, OfficeQA Pro, and LongSeal, with median latency of 8–11 seconds and costs of $0.016–$0.07 per query — 7–11× cheaper and faster than comparable frontier agents.

Pricing: $0.30 per million input tokens, $0.036 per million cached input (free cache writes), and $0.72 per million output tokens. Mixedbread Search integration has a special rate. Toast 1 is backend-agnostic and works via API, coding agents (OpenCode, npx skills), and Mixedbread Stores. It is available immediately with $5 in included credits.

title: New Lower and Upper Bounds for the Grothendieck Constant
summary:
Researchers establish new bounds on the Grothendieck constant \(K_G\):
\[
\frac{6\pi}{11} \le K_G \le \frac{\pi}{2\log(1+\sqrt2)} - 10^{-4}.
\]
The lower bound is achieved by a novel method: instead of constructing explicit gap instances, they show limitations on asymptotically optimal Krivine schemes. The upper bound comes from the first asymptotic construction of rounding schemes, whereas prior work only considered low-dimensional schemes. Together, these bounds determine the previously unknown tenths digit of \(K_G\) to be \(7\). The results were discovered through a long-running collaboration between humans and a long-horizon AI research system. The paper is available on arXiv (2608.11158) and falls under computational complexity and data structures/algorithms.
chinese_title: 格罗滕迪克常数的新上下界
chinese_summary:
研究人员为格罗滕迪克常数 \(K_G\) 确立了新的界：
\[
\frac{6\pi}{11} \le K_G \le \frac{\pi}{2\log(1+\sqrt2)} - 10^{-4}.
\]
下界通过一种新颖方法实现：他们不构造显式的间隙实例，而是证明渐近最优的Krivine方案存在局限。上界来自舍入方案的首次渐近构造，而先前的工作仅考虑了低维方案。这些界共同确定了 \(K_G\) 此前未知的十分位数字为 \(7\)。这些结果是通过人类与一个长周期AI研究系统之间的长期合作发现的。该论文可在arXiv（2608.11158）上获取，主题属于计算复杂性以及数据结构/算法。

title: Ultraviolet Bird Photography
summary:
The article showcases ultraviolet (UV) bird photography, revealing colors invisible to humans. By combining visible and UV images, photographer Nathan Chronister illustrates how birds may perceive their world.

Key points include:

- **Anna's hummingbird** throat feathers reflect both red and UV light, creating a hidden color dimension; unlike the ruby-throated hummingbird, whose throat does not reflect UV. This may help species recognition.
- **Flamingo** reflects UV; red on some blackbirds appears dark in UV due to different pigments.
- **Yellow pigments vary**: the plush-crested jay's yellow belly reflects UV, appearing pink in combined photos, while its yellow eye does not—so birds see them as different colors. A toucan's yellow is UV-dark, but bare facial skin reflects some UV.
- **Dotted patterns** can show UV reflectance without altering visible colors.
- In a **goldfinch and chicory flower**, the bird's back is more UV-reflective than cheek or belly.
- **Blue feathers** are usually structural, with UV following blue reflectance (e.g., western bluebird, indigo bunting). But the **blue-bellied roller** has a belly that is dark blue yet bright in UV, and a **trogon's** blue back reflects little UV, appearing green combined.
- **White feathers** always reflect UV; black/brown feathers are UV-dark. The red-bellied woodpecker’s pattern looks the same in both lights.
- A **green-winged macaw's** beak and facial skin look similar to humans but differ in UV. A **budgerigar** has a UV-reflective chin patch, and its yellow head feathers absorb UV, unlike most yellow feathers.

Overall, UV photography reveals that many bird species have hidden color patterns important for communication and identification.

title: Show HN: Mole – Deep research agent for your terminal
summary:
Mole is a deep-research agent that runs as a single static binary in the terminal, using your own API keys and speaking MCP. It answers questions by decomposing them, searching, reading sources, extracting claims, verifying those claims against their source text, and writing cited answers.

Three core differentiators:

- **Enforced budget**: Every model call is reserved against a budget before it happens and settled after, with non-negative constraints in the database schema. A `--usd 0.50` cap means the run stops at fifty cents; measured overshoot is 0%.
- **Verified quotes**: Every claim carries a verbatim quote that is checked against the page it was mined from. Unsupported claims are discarded at extraction; those that later fail re-reading are marked in the report rather than dropped.
- **Privacy boundary**: Local CSV/folder analysis keeps data on-machine — the model only picks templates and column names, mole renders and runs SQL, and only aggregates (counts, means, buckets of 5+ records) leave.

Install options include a curl script, Homebrew, the AUR, a .deb/.rpm, and `go install`. Configuration uses `~/.config/mole/config.json` (mode 0600) for search (Tavily/Brave) and LLM (Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) providers.

Usage covers one-off research with dollar or token budgets, follow-up questions via sessions, dataset construction with merging across sources, and local data analysis. `mole serve` provides MCP access; `--toolkit` mode inverts control so a coding agent's own model does reasoning while mole supplies deterministic operations like quote checking and SQL rendering.

Self-evaluation shows 0% budget overshoot, 100% claim integrity and citation accuracy, 80% grounding rate, and 70% contradiction precision. Licensed Apache-2.0.

title: Open WireGuard Endpoints
summary:
Proxylity’s UDP Gateway adds two features: open WireGuard endpoints and asynchronous Lambda invocation.

**Open WireGuard Endpoints** – Previously, all WireGuard clients had to be pre-registered via their public keys in CloudFormation. The new `AllowUnknownPeers` property lets a Listener accept handshakes from any valid WireGuard client, while still encrypting the connection. This mirrors HTTPS: transport is encrypted, and identity is handled at the application layer. For extra control, `UnknownPeerPreSharedKey` adds a shared credential gate—unknown peers must include the PSK or the handshake fails. Named peers with per-peer secrets can coexist with this open mode.

**Lambda Async Invocation** – Lambda destinations previously used synchronous `RequestResponse` invocation, waiting for the function to return so replies could be sent. The new `UseAsyncInvoke` argument switches to Lambda’s `Event` mode: the Gateway delivers the packet batch, receives HTTP 202, and moves on. No reply is sent to the client. This suits durable workflows that start long-running processing (e.g., via Step Functions) and don’t need an immediate response. Note: no replies, AWS retries up to twice (idempotency or DLQ needed), and async cannot be combined with response streaming.

**Combined** – A public WireGuard endpoint can trigger a long-running backend workflow: devices generate keys, connect with the shared PSK, and send a packet that launches a Step Functions state machine (provisioning, audit, commands). No key pre-registration or open connection is required.

Both features are available now, default to existing behavior, and require no changes to current listeners or destinations.

title: Maximizing the value of your Claude Code sessions
summary:
Here's a concise summary of the article:

**The core insight:** In Claude Code, task costs vary based on how you run sessions. Efficiency isn't about using fewer tokens overall—it's about ensuring tokens go toward what you actually asked for.

**What decides token price:**
- **Model:** Larger models cost more; use them for hard/ambiguous problems, smaller ones for routine work.
- **Input vs. output:** Output (decode) costs ~5x input (prefill), since output is generated one token at a time.
- **Prompt caching:** Cache reads cost 0.1x input price; writes cost up to 2x. The cache is keyed on model, effort level, and fast mode—so switching `/model`, `/effort`, or fast mode mid-conversation busts the cache and triggers a full re-prefill. Set these at the start.

**Reducing tokens in context:**
- Everything Claude reads or commands output is resent every subsequent turn—cached but still adding context.
- **@-mention files** instead of naming paths—the file is attached directly, saving a Read call or search.
- **Add quiet flags** to noisy commands (test runners, builds) to limit output flooding the conversation.
- Run `/context` in a fresh session to see what's loaded (CLAUDE.md, MCP tools) and cut unnecessary items.

**Session hygiene:**
- Run `/clear` between unrelated tasks; `/compact` when earlier parts of a long task are done. Compact is much cheaper while the conversation is still cached.
- `/rewind` only cuts turns off the end (costs nothing), while `/compact` rewrites the whole conversation.
- Cache expires after 1 hour (subscription) or 5 minutes (API key)—compact before breaks.
- Run `/loop` or subagents in fresh sessions: subagents keep their work out of your main context, returning only their final answer—worth it for large/noisy tasks, overhead for small ones.
chinese_title: 最大化你的Claude Code会话价值
chinese_summary:
以下是这篇文章的简要总结：

**核心观点：** 在 Claude Code 中，任务成本会因你运行会话的方式而异。效率并不在于总体上使用更少的 token，而在于确保 token 用在你实际要求的内容上。

**决定 token 价格的因素：**
- **模型：** 较大的模型成本更高；可将它们用于困难/模糊的问题，较小的模型用于日常任务。
- **输入与输出：** 输出（解码）的成本约为输入（预填充）的 5 倍，因为输出是一个 token 一个 token 生成的。
- **提示缓存：** 缓存读取成本为输入价格的 0.1 倍；写入成本最高可达 2 倍。缓存以模型、努力程度和快速模式为键——因此，在对话中途切换 `/model`、`/effort` 或快速模式会使缓存失效，并触发完全重新预填充。请在开始时设置好这些参数。

**减少上下文中的 token：**
- Claude 读取的所有内容以及命令输出都会在后续每一轮中重新发送——虽然会被缓存，但仍会增加上下文长度。
- **使用 @提及文件**，而不是写出路径——文件会被直接附加，从而省去一次 Read 调用或搜索。
- **为高输出命令（如测试运行器、构建）添加静默标志**，以限制输出淹没对话。
- 在新会话中运行 `/context`，查看加载了哪些内容（CLAUDE.md、MCP 工具），并移除不必要的项目。

**会话卫生：**
- 在无关任务之间运行 `/clear`；当长任务的早期部分已完成时运行 `/compact`。在对话仍处于缓存状态时，压缩会便宜得多。
- `/rewind` 只会从末尾裁剪对话轮次（不产生成本），而 `/compact` 会重写整个对话。
- 缓存会在 1 小时（订阅）或 5 分钟（API 密钥）后过期——休息前请先进行压缩。
- 在新会话中运行 `/loop` 或子代理：子代理会将其工作内容排除在主上下文之外，只返回最终答案——对于大型/高噪声任务来说值得，对于小型任务则是额外开销。

title: Turbo Pascal on CP/M, MSX-DOS and MS-DOS – Pascal for Small Machines
summary:
The article covers Turbo Pascal for small machines, especially MSX, CP/M, and MS-DOS. It begins with Pascal’s namesake Blaise Pascal and its creator Niklaus Wirth, noting Pascal’s goals of structured teaching and efficient implementation. Borland’s Turbo Pascal became hugely popular; version 3 was the last for CP/M, while DOS versions evolved into Borland Pascal 7 and later Delphi/Kylix.

For MSX, Turbo Pascal 3.01 for CP/M was distributed, including by Philips, with an MSX version. Scans of manuals and a patched MSX-2 version by Frits Hilderink (with GIOS) are available. Turbo Pascal 3.3f and the DataBASE Toolkit 1.2 are mentioned, along with freeware PC versions 3.01/3.02.

Since Turbo Pascal lacks direct MSX hardware access, many include-file libraries were created. These include Graphpak, Beunsoft BIOS files, Turbo-Lib, MDL-LIB 2.2, Kari Lammassaari’s support files, Erik Maas’s RS232/fossil interface, and an IDE called MSX PAD by Slotman. Libraries for INL’s TCP/IP stack and Hans Otten’s filter/split programs are also covered. Tools convert MSX screens to PCX and vice versa (CNVS, MSX12CNV, MSXCNV12), and there are Windows converters.

The article lists many Pascal programming resources: inline code generators (INLINE, INLASS, PMLINE), programs for BDOS calls, file splitting, inverse characters, a file manager (SDOS), and digitizing software. It also catalogs magazine articles from MCCM, MSX Club Magazine, and CUC journals, covering Pascal courses, graphics, recursion, hybrid programming, and libraries. Overall, it’s an archive of Turbo Pascal software, documentation, and community contributions for MSX and related systems.
chinese_title: Turbo Pascal在CP/M、MSX-DOS和MS-DOS上——小型机器的Pascal

title: Jason Arday: Former Cambridge university professor found dead
summary:
Jason Arday, the former University of Cambridge professor who resigned amid a plagiarism row, has died at age 41. Emergency services found him unresponsive at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday afternoon. He was pronounced dead at the scene; his next of kin have been informed. Police said his death is being treated as unexpected but is not believed to be suspicious.

Arday resigned last week as Cambridge professor of sociology of education after allegations of plagiarism and questions over some achievements. He denied the claims but admitted errors in his work, saying the controversy had caused “an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack.” The row began when Nathan Cofnas, a self-defined “race realist” who was sacked from Cambridge in 2024, said he found numerous instances of plagiarism and questioned Arday’s achievements.

Arday’s 2023 appointment as Cambridge’s youngest-ever black professor had been widely celebrated. In his resignation statement, he said the “personal cost” had become “too great” and that the scrutiny went “far beyond scholarly disagreement,” but stressed his resignation should not be seen as acceptance of the narratives around him.

Liverpool John Moores University, which awarded Arday his PhD, concluded he had not plagiarised his thesis or journal publications. Earlier this week, Cambridge announced an independent investigation into his appointment. Vice-chancellor Professor Deborah Prentice said the university was “desperately saddened” and sent sympathies to his family and friends.

title: Don't classify, hallucinate
summary:
A common LLM classification task—mapping search queries to a large, fixed taxonomy—is often solved with structured outputs that constrain the model to a list of legal categories. This works but is expensive: you must send the entire vocabulary (hundreds of classes) with every request, and it may exceed context limits.

The article proposes a cheaper, clever alternative: instead of forcing the LLM to choose from real categories, ask a small, "dumb" model to **hallucinate** plausible classifications for the query. For example, for "brown coffee table" the model might invent "Furniture / Living Room / Tables / Coffee"—something that doesn't exist in the real taxonomy.

That fake output is still useful. By precomputing embeddings for all real categories (using something like MiniLM), you can embed the hallucinated classification and find the most similar real category via vector similarity (e.g., dot product). The fake "Furniture / Living Room / Tables / Coffee" resolves to "Furniture / Living Room Furniture / Coffee Tables & End Tables / Coffee Tables."

Benefits: you don't need to ship the full schema to the LLM every time, and you can use smaller/cheaper models for generation. The real taxonomy is only handled locally through embeddings. The author demonstrates this with the Wayfair WANDS dataset and provides a notebook/utility. The post concludes with a plug for "Vectors Week" events on vector retrieval and databases.
chinese_title: 不要分类，要幻觉
chinese_summary:
一个常见的LLM分类任务——将搜索查询映射到一个大型固定分类体系——通常通过结构化输出来解决，即限制模型只能从合法类别列表中选择。这种方法有效但代价高昂：每次请求都必须发送整个词汇表（数百个类别），而且可能超出上下文限制。

文章提出了一种更便宜、更聪明的替代方案：不强迫LLM从真实类别中选择，而是让一个小型“笨”模型为查询**凭空臆造**看似合理的分类。例如，对于“棕色咖啡桌”，模型可能会编造出“家具 / 客厅 / 桌子 / 咖啡”——这个类别在真实分类体系中并不存在。

这个虚假输出仍然有用。通过预先为所有真实类别计算嵌入（例如使用MiniLM），你可以对臆造的分类进行嵌入，并通过向量相似度（如点积）找到最相似的真实类别。虚假的“家具 / 客厅 / 桌子 / 咖啡”会解析为“家具 / 客厅家具 / 咖啡桌与边桌 / 咖啡桌”。

好处：你不需要每次都将完整模式发送给LLM，而且可以使用更小/更便宜的模型来生成。真实分类体系只在本地通过嵌入处理。作者用Wayfair WANDS数据集演示了这一点，并提供了笔记本/工具。文章最后还推广了关于向量检索与数据库的“Vectors Week”活动。

title: Show HN: LuaCAD – Parametric CAD Scripted in Lua
summary:
LuaCAD is a scriptable CAD tool that lets users write parametric 2D and 3D models in Lua and export them to 3MF, STL, OBJ, PLY, OFF, AMF, or SCAD, or render to PNG. It embeds Lua 5.4 in a Rust engine, evaluating CSG operations directly via Manifold or generating OpenSCAD code for external rendering.

The project highlights Lua as an improvement over OpenSCAD’s language: more powerful, consistent, and faster, with operator overloading for natural CSG syntax (`a + b`, `a - b`, `a * b`). Lua is also already used in LibreCAD and Autodesk Netfabb.

Installation options include `cargo install luacad` for the CLI and `luacad-studio` for a GUI with live preview. Both crates vendor C/C++ dependencies, but require a C++ compiler, CMake, and for the GUI, OpenGL development headers.

CLI commands support converting models to various formats (`luacad convert`), rebuilding on file changes (`luacad watch`), rendering to PNG (`luacad render`), showing statistics (`luacad info`), linting with selene (`luacad lint`), and running scripts for side effects (`luacad run`). Format is inferred from the output extension; `--format` overrides, and `--via-openscad` hands off to an installed OpenSCAD binary.

LuaCAD fully reimplements the Belfry OpenSCAD Library v2 (BOSL2), enabling rendering and exports without external dependencies. Text is converted to real geometry via `text()` and `text3d()`. `import()` reads mesh formats and returns solids, while SVG and DXF become 2D sketches ready for extrusion.

Export formats include SCAD, 3MF, STL, OBJ, PLY, OFF, and AMF. Returned values become separate 3MF objects; other formats flatten everything into a single mesh.

title: Forbidden City Cabbage
summary:
The National Palace Museum in Taipei’s star attraction is a small jadeite cabbage carving, known as "Jadeite Cabbage with Insects." Carved from white and green jadeite, it features a realistic cabbage with a katydid and locust in its leaves, using natural flaws to create stem ribs. It occupies its own hall and draws large crowds, though its popularity outpaces its official status—it is designated a "significant antiquity," not a national treasure.

Originally an imperial relic from Beijing’s Forbidden City, it was evacuated during the Japanese invasion and later shipped to Taiwan amid the Chinese Civil War. Its symbolism—linked to female purity, fertility, and dowry tradition—adds to its appeal, though historians note few written records exist. Its fame grew after a 1968 postage stamp and its inclusion in an informal trio of museum treasures, nicknamed "pickled cabbage pork hotpot," alongside the Meat-Shaped Stone and the Mao Kung Ting bronze vessel.

The cabbage is heavily secured, displayed in reinforced glass and escorted when traveling. It rarely goes abroad: after a 2014 trip to Japan, it was loaned to the Czech Republic in August 2025—a move Beijing criticized as "separatist maneuvers," while Taiwan called it cultural exchange. The exhibition in Prague proceeded, marking its first European appearance. The article concludes that the cabbage is now back on display in Taipei, remaining a beloved but historically enigmatic masterpiece.
chinese_title: 故宫白菜
chinese_summary:
台北故宫博物院的镇馆之宝是一件小巧的翠玉白菜雕刻，名为“翠玉白菜”。这件作品以白绿相间的翡翠雕成，白菜造型栩栩如生，菜叶间藏有螽斯和蝗虫，工匠巧妙利用天然瑕疵雕出菜梗脉络。它拥有独立展厅，吸引大量游客参观，尽管其人气远超其官方地位——被列为“重要古物”而非“国宝”。

这件文物原为北京故宫的宫廷藏品，在日本侵华期间被疏散转移，后于国共内战期间运抵台湾。其象征意义——与女性纯洁、多子多福及嫁妆传统相关——更添其魅力，不过历史学家指出相关文献记载甚少。它的名声在1968年登上邮票后大噪，并被列入非正式的“故宫三宝”组合，与“肉形石”和“毛公鼎”并称，被戏称为“酸菜白肉锅”。

这颗白菜安保措施严密，陈列于强化玻璃展柜中，外展时全程护送。它很少出国展出：继2014年赴日展出后，2025年8月又借展捷克共和国——此举被北京批评为“分离主义操弄”，而台湾方面则称之为文化交流。布拉格展览如期举行，标志着其首次在欧洲亮相。文章最后指出，这颗白菜目前已回到台北重新展出，始终是一件备受喜爱却充满历史谜团的杰作。

title: Moving integer division to floating-point is trivial
summary:
The article argues that integer division and remainder can sometimes be efficiently replaced with floating-point operations, despite integer division’s poor latency/throughput on current hardware.

For unsigned or signed integers that fit within the mantissa precision (53 bits for double, 24 bits for single), convert them to floating point and compute:

- quotient: `d = trunc(x / y)`
- remainder: `m = -fma(d, y, -x)` (fused multiply-add required)

This works in the default rounding mode: round-to-nearest, ties-to-even.

Key insight: for binary floating-point division with operands converted exactly, ties in rounding never occur. A tie would require an exact midpoint between representable values, but floating-point division in base 2 has zero midpoints. Thus only the round-to-nearest rule matters.

To prove no incorrect rounding, the article examines the fractional part of `x/y`. If the result has `r` fractional bits, rounding up to the next integer would require at least `r+1` leading ones in the exact fraction. The maximum possible fraction from legal inputs is bounded: the lower bound `(2^r - 1)/2^r` gives exactly `r` leading ones, and the upper bound like `(2^(r+1)-2)/(2^(r+1)-1)` still cannot reach `r+1` ones. So the fractional part is never large enough to round the integer part upward.

Practical considerations:

- Signed integers have smaller magnitudes, so unsigned is the harder case.
- Setting rounding mode is expensive; some hardware supports division with explicit rounding, e.g. AVX-512 `_mm_div_round_sd`.
- Converting int to float and back has a cost, especially for unsigned on x86.
- SIMD can amortize overhead.
- Constant divisors are optimized by compilers; runtime repeated divisors can use tools like libdivide.
- There are formally verified methods for 32/64-bit integer division using double-precision floats.
chinese_title: 将整数除法转换为浮点运算是很简单的。
chinese_summary:
本文认为，整数除法和取余有时可以高效地替换为浮点运算，尽管在当前硬件上整数除法的延迟/吞吐量表现不佳。

对于能落入尾数精度范围内（双精度为53位，单精度为24位）的无符号或有符号整数，将它们转换为浮点数并计算：

- 商：`d = trunc(x / y)`
- 余数：`m = -fma(d, y, -x)`（需要融合乘加）

这在默认舍入模式下有效：舍入到最近，平局时取偶。

关键洞察：对于操作数被精确转换的二进制浮点除法，舍入中永远不会出现平局。平局需要可表示值之间的精确中点，但基数为2的浮点除法不存在中点。因此只需考虑舍入到最近规则。

为了证明不存在错误舍入，本文考察`x/y`的小数部分。如果结果有`r`个小数位，向上舍入到下一个整数需要精确小数部分中至少有`r+1`个前导1。合法输入可能产生的最大分数是有界的：下界`(2^r - 1)/2^r`恰好给出`r`个前导1，而上界如`(2^(r+1)-2)/(2^(r+1)-1)`仍然无法达到`r+1`个1。因此小数部分永远不会大到足以将整数部分向上舍入。

实际考虑：

- 有符号整数的量级更小，因此无符号是更困难的情形。
- 设置舍入模式代价高昂；某些硬件支持带有显式舍入的除法，例如AVX-512 `_mm_div_round_sd`。
- 将整数转换为浮点再转换回来有成本，尤其是在x86上处理无符号整数时。
- SIMD可以分摊开销。
- 编译器会对常量除数进行优化；对于运行时重复使用的除数，可以使用libdivide等工具。
- 已有使用双精度浮点数进行32/64位整数除法的形式化验证方法。

title: The TEMU-Fication of Software, Digital Goods and Services
summary:
The article argues that digital goods—software, books, music, articles, and streaming content—are undergoing a "TEMU-fication": becoming cheaper, more abundant, and noticeably worse, while human-made work shifts into a luxury tier. Just as fast fashion externalizes costs onto cheap labor and low quality, AI models compress the historical labor of programmers, writers, and artists, producing near-zero-marginal-cost output that is "just barely good enough."

Key manifestations include:
- **Vibe-coded software**: AI-generated code often fails security tests, introduces vulnerabilities, and compounds technical debt, especially when users can't recognize quality.
- **AI-written books**: An estimated 10,000–40,000 AI-generated books hit Amazon monthly, flooding categories like travel guides and health with inaccurate or fabricated content.
- **AI-generated articles and video**: Over half of new online articles are AI-generated; YouTube channels feature increasing AI slop, especially on Shorts.
- **AI music**: Platforms like Spotify remove millions of spam tracks, yet the economics still favor AI-generated filler.

There is some pushback—engagement with AI content has dropped, and humans still get more traffic—but the author sees it as a delay, not a limit. Using Netflix as a case study, he predicts that within 5–10 years, a basic subscription tier will feature mostly AI-generated procedural content, with targeted ads injected in real time, while a premium tier will explicitly offer human-made work as a luxury product.

The author concludes by comparing this to the handmade goods market: industrialization didn't eliminate artisans but created a premium niche. Similarly, human-made software, writing, and art may survive as a smaller, high-value segment.
chinese_title: 软件、数字商品与服务的TEMU化
chinese_summary:
文章认为，数字商品——软件、书籍、音乐、文章和流媒体内容——正在经历一场“TEMU化”：变得更便宜、更丰富，但质量明显下降，而人工创作的作品则转向奢侈层级。正如快时尚将成本外部化到廉价劳动力和低质量上，AI模型压缩了程序员、作家和艺术家的历史劳动，产出近乎零边际成本、且“刚好够用”的内容。

主要表现包括：
- **随性编码软件**：AI生成的代码经常无法通过安全测试，引入漏洞，并加剧技术债务，尤其是当用户无法辨别质量时。
- **AI撰写的书籍**：据估计，每月有1万至4万本AI生成的书籍上架亚马逊，旅游指南和健康等类别被不准确或捏造的内容淹没。
- **AI生成的文章和视频**：超过一半的新在线文章由AI生成；YouTube频道中AI垃圾内容越来越多，尤其是在Shorts短视频中。
- **AI音乐**：Spotify等平台下架了数百万首垃圾曲目，但经济逻辑仍然偏向AI生成的填充性音乐。

虽然也存在一些抵制——人们对AI内容的参与度有所下降，人类创作的内容仍能获得更多流量——但作者认为这只是延迟，而非限制。他以Netflix为案例研究，预测在未来5到10年内，基础订阅层将主要包含AI生成的程序化内容，并实时插入定向广告，而高级订阅层则将明确把人工创作的作品作为奢侈品提供。

作者最后将其与手工艺品市场进行类比：工业化并未消灭手工艺人，而是创造了一个高端利基市场。同样，人工创作的软件、写作和艺术可能会以更小但高价值的细分市场存续下去。

title: In Australia, a home battery boom has helped cut wholesale power prices
summary:
Australia’s program to subsidize home batteries has driven a major boom, with more than 500,000 systems installed since July 2025. Energy Minister Chris Bowen said Australia now has more home batteries than the United States, despite the U.S. having 12 times the population. The initiative is part of a broader effort to use surplus rooftop solar power, which often goes to waste and can destabilize the grid by forcing centralized plants offline and plunging prices.

To address excess generation, the government has also offered free power in the early afternoon in some states, encouraging consumers to run appliances or charge EVs. title: A Contract-Grade Verifier for LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
summary:
The paper proposes a stricter correctness verification method for LLM-generated GPU kernels. The authors argue that current systems report high correctness rates based on loose tests—running kernels on a few random inputs at one fixed shape and comparing outputs to a reference with tolerance. Such tests can miss serious failures: returning ordinary numbers when true results are NaN or infinite, nondeterministic behavior, shape-sensitivity, and fp16 accumulation where the reference maintains fp32 precision.

To address this, they build a “contract-grade” verifier with twelve adversarial properties, several tolerance-free, so failures cannot be dismissed by threshold choices. They apply it to 2,638 machine-generated kernels already accepted by a public system’s harness. The verifier finds 39.5% broken beyond any tolerance argument and 62.1% with at least one violation. Importantly, the standard test accepted 1,487 kernels that the verifier rejects, while only 14 were rejected by the standard test and accepted by the verifier. They defend these findings through four checks: a 7/7 positive control, a threshold-calibration sweep, 98.5% agreement with the reference benchmark’s own correctness code, and a stratified hand-audit.

They also use the verifier on their own kernel: the first native Blackwell tcgen05 training backward for the gated-linear-recurrence (GDN) family, including the reverse-state stage previously run on a fallback. Its correctness is established against a double-precision oracle, and five family members are trained through it.

Overall, the authors conclude that reported correctness signals in LLM-generated kernel systems are far weaker than the numbers suggest, and tolerance-free contract-based verification could close much of the gap.

title: Gödel, Escher, Elisp: The Beauty of Macros
summary:
Based on the title and its likely themes, the article *“Gödel, Escher, Elisp: The Beauty of Macros”* appears to explore Lisp/Emacs Lisp macros through the same lens as Douglas Hofstadter’s *Gödel, Escher, Bach*.

The main point is that macros are a form of **metaprogramming**: they let programmers write code that writes code. Unlike ordinary functions, which operate on values, macros operate on source-code structures before evaluation. This gives the programmer a way to extend the language itself, creating new syntax and control constructs.

The Gödel connection likely highlights **self-reference and formal systems**. Gödel’s incompleteness theorems showed how formal systems can make statements about themselves; similarly, Lisp macros allow programs to manipulate their own code as data. This is possible because Lisp is **homoiconic**—code and data share the same list-based structure.

Escher’s artwork, with its recursive staircases and interlocking figures, parallels the way macros blur the boundary between **program and data**, **runtime and compile-time**, and **inside and outside** the program. Macros create “strange loops” where levels of language fold into one another.

The article likely argues that macros are beautiful not just because they are powerful, but because they reveal deep connections between computation, mathematics, and art. It probably also cautions that this beauty carries a cost: macros can make code harder to read, debug, and reason about. Their true beauty lies in the elegance they can produce when used with restraint and imagination.

In short, the article presents macros as both a practical tool and a philosophical idea—demonstrating that programming, like mathematics and art, can express deeply recursive and self-referential structures.
chinese_title: 哥德尔、埃舍尔、Elisp：宏之美
chinese_summary:
根据标题及其可能涉及的主题，文章《哥德尔、埃舍尔与Elisp：宏之美》似乎以道格拉斯·霍夫施塔特的《哥德尔、埃舍尔、巴赫》相同的视角来探讨Lisp/Emacs Lisp宏。

核心观点是，宏是元编程的一种形式：它让程序员能够编写生成代码的代码。与操作值的普通函数不同，宏在求值之前操作源代码结构。这为程序员提供了一种扩展语言本身的方式，创造出新的语法和控制结构。

与哥德尔的关联可能凸显了自指和形式系统。哥德尔的不完备定理展示了形式系统如何对自身做出陈述；类似地，Lisp宏允许程序将自身代码作为数据进行操作。这之所以可能，是因为Lisp具有同像性——代码和数据共享相同的基于列表的结构。

埃舍尔的艺术作品，以其递归的阶梯和交错的图形，与宏模糊程序与数据、运行时与编译时、程序内部与外部之间界限的方式相似。宏创造了“怪圈”，使语言的各个层次相互折叠。

文章很可能认为，宏之所以美，不仅因为其强大，更在于它们揭示了计算、数学与艺术之间的深层联系。它可能还告诫，这种美是有代价的：宏可能使代码更难阅读、调试和推理。宏真正的美在于，当以克制和想象力使用时，它们所展现出的优雅。

简而言之，文章将宏既视为一种实用工具，又视为一种哲学理念——表明编程如同数学和艺术一样，能够表达深层的递归与自指结构。

title: High-Performance Array-Backed LRU Hash Table
summary:
This article describes a high-performance concurrent LRU hash table designed for multi-core, NUMA, and low-latency environments. It replaces standard library containers (e.g., `std::unordered_map` + `std::list` with a global lock) which suffer from lock convoying, pointer chasing, allocator overhead, and false sharing.

**Core architecture highlights:**
- **Sharded parallelism:** Independent shards each with a TTAS spinlock, hash buckets, and LRU chain, scaled to ~CPU cores × 32.
- **Zero runtime allocations:** Pre-allocated flat “Mega-Blocks” of nodes and buckets; 32-bit indices replace 64-bit pointers to halve structural memory overhead.
- **Cache-friendly layout:** Nodes separate hot-path fields (hash, chain indices, key) into the first cache line and cold-path data (value pointer, LRU metadata) into secondary lines, minimizing memory fetches.
- **NUMA awareness:** Shard allocations distributed across sockets (via `VirtualAllocExNuma` or libnuma).
- **Advanced concurrency:** Out-of-lock destruction of evicted payloads avoids latency spikes; lazy LRU promotion uses a generation counter to skip upgrades on hot reads, boosting throughput ~20%.
- **Adaptive spin policies:** TTAS with exponential backoff; kernel-mode uses `EX_PUSH_LOCK`.

**Benchmarks:**
- Under heavy multi-threaded mixed workloads, the array table scales positively (e.g., 7.51× speedup at 20 threads on i7-12700H) while the std implementation exhibits negative scaling (0.49×).
- Tail latencies are dramatically improved: P99.9 up to 360× more stable; P99.99 up to 212× more stable compared to std.
- Total throughput speedup ranges from ~8.9× (mobile 4-core) to ~20.9× (hybrid 14-core).
- Lazy promotion yields up to 20% higher throughput in 95/5 read/write workloads.

The design is suitable for HFT, storage caches, network routing, kernel drivers, and web servers.
chinese_title: 高性能数组实现LRU哈希表
chinese_summary:

**核心架构亮点：**
- **分片并行：** 每个独立分片都配有 TTAS 自旋锁、哈希桶和 LRU 链，分片数量约为 CPU 核心数 × 32。
- **零运行时分配：** 预先分配由节点和桶组成的扁平“巨型块”（Mega-Blocks）；用 32 位索引替代 64 位指针，使结构内存开销减半。
- **缓存友好布局：** 节点将热路径字段（哈希、链索引、键）放入第一个缓存行，将冷路径数据（值指针、LRU 元数据）放入次要缓存行，从而最大限度减少内存获取。
- **NUMA 感知：** 分片分配分布在各个 socket 上（通过 `VirtualAllocExNuma` 或 libnuma）。
- **高级并发：** 在锁外销毁被逐出的负载，避免延迟尖峰；惰性 LRU 提升使用代际计数器来跳过热读路径上的升级操作，吞吐量提升约 20%。
- **自适应自旋策略：** TTAS 带指数退避；内核态使用 `EX_PUSH_LOCK`。

**基准测试：**
- 在重度多线程混合负载下，该数组表展现出正向扩展（例如在 i7-12700H 上 20 线程时加速比达 7.51 倍），而标准库实现则呈现负扩展（0.49 倍）。
- 尾部延迟得到显著改善：与标准库相比，P99.9 稳定性最高提升 360 倍；P99.99 稳定性最高提升 212 倍。
- 总吞吐量加速比范围约为 8.9 倍（移动端 4 核）到 20.9 倍（混合 14 核）。
- 在 95/5 读写负载下，惰性提升可带来最高 20% 的吞吐量提升。

该设计适用于高频交易（HFT）、存储缓存、网络路由、内核驱动程序和 Web 服务器。

title: Earth.nullschool.net
summary:

title: Firefox is now the last major browser that still supports uBlock Origin
summary: Firefox says it will continue supporting uBlock Origin, making it the last major browser to do so. Microsoft Edge is moving to Manifest V3, which blocks ad-blocking extensions from accessing the functions needed to block ads effectively. Edge follows Google’s lead since it is Chromium-based, as are Opera, Brave, Vivaldi, and Samsung Browser. Firefox is one of the few non-Chromium browsers, and unlike Safari and DuckDuckGo, it still supports uBlock Origin. For users who want full ad-blocking, Firefox is the only browser without compromise; other browsers require uBlock Origin Lite or built-in ad-blocking with fewer features.

chinese_summary: Firefox表示将继续支持uBlock Origin，使其成为最后一个这样做的主流浏览器。微软Edge正在转向Manifest V3，该版本会阻止广告拦截扩展访问有效拦截广告所需的功能。Edge追随谷歌的步伐，因为它基于Chromium，Opera、Brave、Vivaldi和三星浏览器也是如此。Firefox是少数非Chromium浏览器之一，与Safari和DuckDuckGo不同，它仍然支持uBlock Origin。对于想要完整广告拦截功能的用户来说，Firefox是唯一无妥协的浏览器；其他浏览器则需要使用功能较少的uBlock Origin Lite或内置广告拦截。

title: HashAgent – Share an AI agent as a URL, runs locally via WebGPU
summary: HashAgent is a tool that lets you package an AI agent into a single shareable URL. The key idea is that the entire agent runs locally in your browser using WebGPU, rather than on remote servers. This makes AI interactions private: user data and model execution stay on-device. Sharing is simplified—passing a URL is enough, with no installation, accounts, or backend setup required. WebGPU enables accelerated machine-learning inference directly in the browser, allowing useful AI performance without cloud computing. The tagline “Private AI in one URL” captures the core benefits: privacy, portability, and ease of distribution.
